paragraphs: Friend, here's what this psalm is really about. The fool says in his heart, "There is no God," and then David shows where that road ends: "They are corrupt; their acts are vile." (Psalm 14:1) A heart that shuts God out doesn't stay quiet for long, because it leaks into what a person does. Then David makes it bigger: "All have turned away, they have together become corrupt; there is no one who does good, not even one." (Psalm 14:3)

Now hold on, because David isn't only looking at people. The LORD "looks down from heaven upon the sons of men to see if any understand, if any seek God." (Psalm 14:2) I think that's the heart of it, baker: He's looking for anyone who will seek Him. And if you see yourself in that crowd who turned away, hear this: it's not a reason to hide from Him, it's a reason to seek Him.

So where does that leave us? David says God "is in the company of the righteous," and "the LORD is their shelter." (Psalm 14:5-6) When the world feels crooked, God hasn't gone anywhere. David ends with a big "Oh, that the salvation of Israel would come from Zion!" and calls for joy when the LORD restores His captive people (Psalm 14:7), and that's why my ovens stay ready, friend: we keep seeking Him, we take shelter in Him, and we wait for that joy.
